summary: The game does not use src/render3d/character.js. That file is only imported by the room tool (src/main.js:13 and :405, index.html). The in-game protagonist and mascot are built entirely inside src/game/room_view.js: makePerson (7525) and makeMascot (7991). game.html creates them through roomView.setCharacter('jachwi') and then setCharacter('moni') (game.html:12132-12139). The protagonist is 'jachwi' → asset id 'jachwi_f' (room_view.js:7297). Its mesh and idle clip come from one file, assets/characters/3d/lq/char_jachwi_f_idle.glb (2.43 MB, 15,832 verts, 24-bone rig, 1 material + PNG). Walking comes from assets/derived/char_clips/char_jachwi_f_walking.glb (35 KB, clip only). Actions come from assets/characters/3d/anim/char_jachwi_f_{opendoor,repot,harvest,harvest_crouch,sit,sleep}.glb. In every file the code takes animations[0] and renames it, so the clip names inside the files do not matter. The file name is the key: idle and walking by file, and ACT_SPEC maps water→opendoor, sow→repot, harvest→harvest or harvest_crouch (target y<0.45), sit→sit, sleep→sleep. There is no runtime scaling. The 1.40 m height (0.375 m for the mascot) is baked into a '__scale_root' wrapper node. The engine keeps the feet on the floor by measuring each clip's lowest skinned vertex at 8 phases (measureGround) and sliding model.position.y toward that value. It also overwrites the Hips bone's local X/Z every frame, so every clip plays in place. Movement moves only root.position x/z. It uses floor_nav (radius 0.38 = BODY_R, 0.25 m grid) through navPathTo → nav.path/pushOut at WALK_SPEED 1.45 m/s. Facing is root.rotation.y = atan2(dx,dz) with local +Z as the front (measured, no π), turning at 9/s, and the character faces the camera on arrival. Sit and lie are 'hold' actions: root snaps to the furniture centre and takes the furniture's yaw, the whole clip plays over 1.2 s or 1.6 s, and the last frame is held. For sit, the root is then lifted so Hips world y equals the seat top (surfaceTopAt). For lie, the root goes to bed top − 0.04. The mascot is a static unrigged mesh (lq/char_mascot_sprout.glb, 242 KB) animated only procedurally: it floats 0.221 m up, bobs 0.103 m on a 2.5 s period, tilts 4°, follows 0.774 m behind the person, and yaws toward the person at 6/s. Both are re-created from scratch on every room re-assemble, including a furniture move (room_view.js:1059-1061, 1166-1171).

constraints: Do not add runtime scaling. Height is baked in the GLB: the person is 1.40 m in bind pose (1.28–1.45 m in idle, test_ground A2) and the mascot is 0.375 m. Use tools/char/rescale_char_glb.py (a '__scale_root' wrapper). Feet at y=0, origin between the feet (XZ≈0). Comments at room_view.js:7282 and 7530 forbid engine rescaling.

The forward axis is local +Z (face and toes) with +Y up, for both the person and the mascot. Yaw = atan2(dx,dz) with no +π (room_view.js:7360-7372, 8070-8074). The sit clip must face +Z. The lie clip must lie on its back along Z with the head toward −Z and the feet toward +Z, because root.rotation.y is set to the furniture's rotation.y (room_view.js:8862).

Bone names are the binding contract. Tracks bind by node name, so the mesh file and every clip file must share one skeleton naming. There must be a node matching /hips/i (the pelvis; its parent must be an unrotated Y-up node, since local X/Z are pinned at 7913) and a node named exactly 'RightHand' after three's name sanitizing (regex /^righthand$/i at 7636). 'mixamorig:RightHand' becomes 'mixamorigRightHand' and fails.

No root motion. Walk and every action clip must be in place. Hips local X/Z is overwritten each frame with the idle t≈0 value (7629-7631, 7913), so root motion on any bone above Hips would make the character drift.

The sleep clip must be a lying pose in all 8 sampled phases, with no stand-to-lie transition. measureGround takes the minimum lowest vertex over the whole clip (7599-7623), and that minimum places the body on the mattress (root = surfaceTop − 0.04).

Sit and lie clips play whole, not subclipped (win:0). They are time-scaled to 1.2 s or 1.6 s and the LAST frame is held (clampWhenFinished, heldAction). Sit then lifts the root so Hips world y = seat top (8876-8879).

Keep the movement numbers unchanged: WALK_SPEED 1.45, ARRIVE_EPS 0.10, BODY_R/nav radius 0.38 (7358, 826), ACT_REACH 1.45, ACT_STAND_R, TURN_RATE 9, MON follow params (7353). They feed reachability/placement probes (probe_reach) and must not move. Only WALK_CLIP_MPS (180) should change, and only to match a new walk clip's measured ground speed.

The watering can attaches to the RightHand bone and compensates for bone world scale (1/hs, 8943-8944). Test N-4 expects the can plus water points during a water act.

risks: Using a new rig with different bone names while reusing the old anim/*.glb files fails silently. PropertyBinding only warns 'No target node', and the character stands in bind pose. All 8 files (idle, walking, opendoor, repot, harvest, harvest_crouch, sit, sleep) must be regenerated on the new skeleton, e.g. Meshy rig + animate on the same model.

A Blender or other Z-up export with a rotated Armature makes the Hips X/Z pin at 7913 pin the wrong axes, including vertical, so the character sinks or levitates. Keep the Hips parent unrotated with Y up, as in the current Armature (scale 0.01, no rotation).

tools/test_ground.mjs E2 requires |idle − walking| ground offset > 0.03 m. That only holds because the current mocap idle floats 8.6 cm and walking sinks 2.8 cm. A clean replacement will FAIL E2 even though it looks correct, so the test must be updated alongside the asset.
WALK_CLIP_MPS 0.871 was measured on the current walk clip. With a new clip and no re-measure, feet visibly slide or the walk looks like running (timeScale = (1.45−0.23)/WALK_CLIP_MPS, clamped ≥0.6).

The ACT_SPEC from/win windows (0.30+1.50 opendoor etc.) were chosen by measuring the hand trajectories of the current clips. New clips without re-measuring put the watering can or hand in the wrong place and the crossfade snaps.

Generated sit/sleep clips that include a stand-to-sit or stand-to-lie transition break the fit. Sleep floats because measureGround takes the minimum over the standing frames. Sit is fine as long as the final frame is seated. A looping seated idle would freeze on its last frame, so there is no breathing while held.

The SSAO/SAO passes (vendor/three/postprocessing/SSAOPass.js:71, SAOPass.js:57-60) render normals and depth with a plain MeshNormalMaterial/MeshDepthMaterial override without skinning, so in r128 the skinned character is drawn in BIND pose in that pass. Result: a ghost of the standing A-pose in the AO, even while sitting or lying. Fix when wiring post-FX: set normalMaterial.skinning = true (and depthMaterial for SAO). This is safe for non-skinned meshes in r128 because skinning also requires maxBones > 0.

Post-FX override passes also draw transparent helper planes (blob shadows at y=0.006, selection rings, walk ghost cylinder) as opaque geometry into the depth/normal buffers. The invisible pick box is skipped because material.visible=false is filtered before the override. Consider excluding these via layers.

Characters are disposed and reloaded on every assemble(), including every furniture move (1059-1061, 1166-1171), and charLoad has no GLB cache. A heavier protagonist (above the current 2.4 MB / 15.8k verts / 1 material) directly lengthens every re-assemble and the first boot. Any per-character material or layer tweak must be applied inside makePerson/makeMascot, not once.

A new height or a non-chibi silhouette leaves several hard-coded visuals sized for 1.40 m: pick box 0.62×1.55×0.62 at y 0.78 (7554), charBodyPos up 0.62 (9107), GHOST_H 1.40 (9017), blob 1.05 (7559), ring 0.26-0.34, CAN_MAX 0.24 (8506). These are UI/visual only, but tap hit-testing depends on the pick box and body anchor.

A rigged, animated mascot would need new mixer/update code. makeMascot has no AnimationMixer and would render a rigged GLB in bind pose. Its follow/bob/yaw logic is transform-only and can stay if the rig plays only an in-place idle.

src/render3d/character.js (room tool) expects lq/char_<id>_rigged.glb + derived/char_clips/char_<id>_idle.glb + walking. If only the game files are replaced, the room tool at index.html keeps showing the old character or 404s.

docs/handoff/char-to-house.md says 'model.rotation.y = Math.PI'. That is wrong for these assets (twice-measured +Z forward). Do not re-add π when swapping models; verify the new model's LeftFoot→LeftToeBase and Head→headfront vectors point +Z (FK check: idle headfront−Head = (0,−0.04,+0.17)).
perf_notes: Renderer: room_view uses scene.js's renderer with pixel ratio min(maxPixelRatio 1.75, dpr) (room_view.js:690, 5319). autoQuality steps it down through [1.75, 1.5, 1.25, 1.0, 0.85] when two consecutive 500 ms busy windows fall below 24 fps (5320-5341). Shadows: PCFShadowMap (not Soft) at 751. Sun shadow map is 1024² with bias +0.0002 (749, 781); the ceiling bulb shadow is 512 (point light, so 6 cube faces). Both characters castShadow=true and receiveShadow=true, so the skinned 15.8k-vert mesh is drawn in every shadow pass as well. The render loop draws on demand (loop 5204-5256, render call 5230 = the single hook for an EffectComposer). Frame-rate caps: idle with no skeletal character 10 fps; idle with the person standing 18 fps (ANIM_IDLE_FPS 5136, drops permanently to 10 on slow devices, idleBackoff); busy (drag, camera tween, rings) 30 fps; person walking or acting 60 fps (drops to 30 via moveBackoff). A person in the room therefore means the scene redraws at least 18 fps forever, so any post-FX chain runs continuously at that rate on phones. Budget SSAO/bloom accordingly, e.g. half-res AO, skip AO while LV_MOVE, or let the character stay idle-only at 10 fps with post-FX. Character update rate equals draw rate (stepCharacters 5190-5202, dt clamped to 0.1). setPaused stops rAF entirely while the plant zoom iframe is open (5269). measureGround runs skinLowestY (220 sampled verts × 8 phases per clip per skinned mesh) once per clip, cached. Multiple skinned sub-meshes in a new character multiply that one-time cost and the per-frame skinning/shadow cost. The current budget worth keeping: protagonist ≤ ~16k verts, 1 material, 1 texture (lq idle GLB 2.43 MB); mascot 5.4k verts, 242 KB. Tested phone target is 390×844 at dpr 2 (tools/test_roomview_perf.mjs, test_perf_budget.mjs).

summary: game.html boots the room with a dynamic `import('./src/game/room_view.js')`, then calls `createRoomView(#roomCanvas, {roomId, lightEngine: io.light, onProgress, onCharacterTap, onPlantTap, onLampTap, lampTapMenu, onSlotTap, onError})` (game.html:11928). It exposes the returned view as `window.__rv` (game.html:12019) and drives it only through view methods. room_view.js (10,144 lines) wraps render3d/scene.js `createScene`/`updateLight` and house.js `buildHouse`. It owns the camera, placement, raycast picking, characters, walk/act animations, lamps and the render loop. It is supposed to know nothing about game rules. Time of day is pushed in from outside. game.html's idle clock (`idleClockStart`, game.html:15564) moves `dayPhase` (0=midnight, 0.25=06:00, one full day = 576 s) and calls `roomView.setDaylight(dayPhase)` on every rAF (game.html:15581). That calls `applyDaylight()` (room_view.js:4900), which runs `updateLight`, applies the game's dimming and boost factors and sets `needsRender`. The clock pauses while `#stage.talking`, while the guide is open, during the day-change animation and when the tab is hidden. The camera is an orbit rig {az, el, dist, target} (room_view.js:878). It changes through `setCam` → an eased `tween` (1558/1602) that `updateCam()` applies once per rendered frame (1614). `focusSlot()` is the only existing zoom-in, and game.html uses it once as a pull-then-return (`focusOnMonstera`, game.html:11044). Rendering is one `ctx.renderer.render(scene, cam)` in `loop()` (5230), plus `redraw()` (9647) and the boot frame (10128). The loop draws only when needed: 10 fps idle (18 with a skinned character), 30 fps busy, 60 fps while moving. There is no post-processing yet. vendor/three/postprocessing, shaders and math are untracked new files and are not loaded by any page. Audio is fully synthesized with WebAudio and ships no audio files. music.js gets a lazily created `musicCtx` from game.html (game.html:11786). sfx.js makes its own lazy AudioContext for its six voices (tap, scrape, water, step, chime, thud). Both follow the single localStorage key `byeot.music`, toggled by the ♪ button (#btnMusic). The '화면 밝기' slider only sets `toneMappingExposure = 0.72 × userBright` through `view.brightness(v)`.

risks: SSAO/SAO depth-normal override pass will draw the 'hidden' walls and ceiling. Cutaway hides them with colorWrite=false/depthWrite=false while keeping visible=true (house.js:1251-1259), and SSAOPass.renderOverride uses scene.overrideMaterial (MeshNormalMaterial), which ignores that. With the camera looking down, the ceiling and camera-facing walls cover the room in the SSAO depth buffer and the AO is lost or wrong. The fix is to set visible=false on colorWrite=false meshes (and to skip glass, heatmap, blob and ghost meshes) only around the normal pass, after the beauty pass has already consumed shadow needsUpdate. Otherwise the sun leaks through the ceiling.

r128 applies tone mapping inside material shaders even when rendering into a render target, but writes LINEAR encoding into targets (outputEncoding comes from the target texture). The composer therefore needs a final GammaCorrection/LinearToSRGB step. With the default 8-bit RGBA targets, a dark basement stored linearly will band badly in the shadows. Use HalfFloatType targets on WebGL2 (with a fallback) or an sRGB-encoded first target.

Rendering into composer targets loses MSAA. Desktop currently gets antialias:true; phones already have AA off (room_view.js:707-713 creates webgl2 with antialias:false when dpr>=2). Add FXAA/SMAA, or WebGLMultisampleRenderTarget on WebGL2 desktop only.

light_grid_labels hookRender (light_grid_labels.js:420-425) and outside.js updateMatrixWorld overrides (outside.js:902, :1192) run on EVERY renderer.render. SSAOPass calls render twice per frame (beauty + normals) and traverses the scene twice to cache visibility. That double-applies the outside day colours, halves the alley-walker warmup, and can trigger its `dt<=0` gap reset (outside.js:910) when timers are coarse. Labels also update several times per frame.

autoQuality (room_view.js:5322-5341) permanently lowers the pixel ratio when busy-window fps < 24 for 1 s. Heavy post work will push phones down to 1.0 or 0.85 and the ratio never recovers. Add post-effect tiers that are dropped before resolution, and keep the composer pixel ratio in sync.

The idle game clock calls setDaylight every rAF (game.html:15581), and applyDaylight sets needsRender=true unconditionally (room_view.js:5040). The room therefore renders at about 30fps continuously while the clock runs, so post-processing cost is paid all the time, not only on interaction. The clock pauses only during dialogue, the guide, the day-transition animation or a hidden tab.

scene.js:107 creates a new THREE.Fog on every updateLight call, which is every frame. In r128 `material.fog && cachedFog !== scene.fog` forces a program-cache-key recomputation for every fog-enabled material every frame, a CPU hotspot that grows with the number of scene renders. Fog near/far is ≥30/120 m (room_view.js:5018-5021), so fog has no visible effect in the room.

Shader light count is large: 1 dir + hemi + ambient + 16 skyPortals SpotLights (intensity 0 for all but one in banjiha) + ceilingBulb + up to 4 lamp-rig PointLights. Every MeshStandardMaterial fragment loops over all of them. That already costs fill rate before post is added. Setting visible=false on unused portals removes them from the shader (visual-only), but changing the light count forces a shader recompile.

Probes and tests measure screen luminance (e.g. floor 103.8, outside darker than floor, lamp pools) and some call r.render(scene, cam) directly (tools/test_perf_budget.mjs:48, :210-214), bypassing the composer. renderer.info resets on every render call, so stats().calls/triangles (room_view.js:9831) would report only the last full-screen pass. perf_notes: Target phone is 390×844 CSS (the PHONE constant, room_view.js:132). The pixel ratio is min(O.maxPixelRatio 1.75, dpr), about 683×1477 ≈ 1.0 Mpx per full-screen pass. autoQuality can step it down through [1.75, 1.5, 1.25, 1.0, 0.85] and never raises it again (room_view.js:5319-5341). The context is webgl2 with antialias:false, alpha:false, stencil:false, high-performance when dpr>=2 (:707-713); desktop keeps scene.js antialias:true. Shadows in the 'lean' budget (default, :4864-4889): only the sun casts. Its map is 1024 (:749) with PCFShadowMap, not Soft (:751), and the shadow camera is tightened to the room (half = max(2.5, diag/2+0.6) ≈ 3.8 m for banjiha, about 7 mm per texel). autoUpdate=false and the map re-renders only when the sun moves more than 0.004 rad (:4976-4984), about every 0.5 s at the normal clock speed. Sky portals and the ceiling bulb do not cast in lean mode. The measured room load is about 103 draw calls and 76k triangles, and a headless render took 1.4 ms (comments at :5061-5062, :5089). Render cadence: idle 10 fps, 18 with a skeletal character idling (ANIM_IDLE_FPS :5136), busy 30 fps (MIN_FRAME_MS :5094), moving 60 fps with backoff to 30 (:5077). Because the idle clock calls setDaylight every rAF, the room normally draws at the busy 30 fps (see risks). setPaused (:5269) stops rAF entirely while plant_grow is open. forceContinuous/setContinuous is used for demos and measurements. Post-processing advice for phones: (1) Fold grade + vignette + gamma + FXAA into ONE ShaderPass, since every full-screen pass costs about 1 Mpx of read and write. (2) Run bloom at half or quarter resolution with a high threshold; tone mapping has already happened in the materials, so bloom sees LDR. (3) SSAO at full resolution is the most expensive option: it re-renders the whole scene for normals and depth and traverses it twice. Prefer half-resolution SAO/SSAO with the hidden-wall handling, or skip AO on phones and rely on the existing blob contact shadows (room_view.js:1203) plus baked or vertex AO. (4) Gate every effect on capability (webgl2, float or half-float render targets, depth texture) and on the autoQuality level, dropping effects before the pixel ratio drops. (5) Use HalfFloat composer targets on WebGL2 to avoid banding in dark areas. (6) Two contexts can be live at once (room + plant_grow iframe), so keep the extra render-target memory small. (7) Dust particles and shaft animation need continuous frames; the clock already supplies about 30 fps, and while it is paused (dialogue) the animation must mark itself as 'moving' in loop() (:5219) the way pulseRings does. Otherwise dust freezes at the 10 fps idle cap.

summary: The game's room (game.html → src/game/room_view.js) is built by render3d/house.js buildHouse(), which walks data/house_rooms.json rooms.banjiha.furniture (11 entries, lines 49-137), merges each with data/furniture_presets.json (`{...preset, ...f}`, house.js:793), and calls the code-only builder furniture_pastel.js buildFurniture(type,p) (1269-1281). That returns a floor-origin THREE.Group of unnamed primitive meshes plus the logical contract on userData: size{w,h,d}, slots[{x,y,z}], tier_heights, tier_max_pot_d, mount, hangFromCeiling, movable, lampShade. Every downstream system uses that userData, not the look. Collision (house.js:813-814 → colliders → floor_nav.js), light-sim occluders (house.js:819-824, OBB from size), plant slots (house.js:928-946, from userData.slots) and lamp rigs (house.js:827-865) are all plain data. The light engine (light_adapter.js:109-168) and 20+ Node tools build the same house headless with no GLTFLoader. room_view renders the SAME `built` object the light engine holds (room_view.js:1083-1086), so adding visual children does not change DLI. BUT room_view's placement layer raycasts the real furniture meshes. surfaceAt (4308-4475), tierRectOf/collectTierRects (3575-3635), surfaceTopAt (6481-6507; used for the heatmap and sit/sleep height at 8858-8861), supportY (2922-2940), pickFurnitureAt (5973-5985) and pickLampRay (4082-4096) all take the plate rectangle from meshRect(hit mesh) (4138-4155), i.e. the hit mesh's local geometry bbox. So a GLB mesh that rays can hit would silently change cell grids, snapping, sit heights and pot fit. The shelf GLBs in assets/furniture/*.glb (28-312 tris, untextured, dimensions differ from the presets) and assets/lamps/*.glb are not loaded anywhere today. Legacy render3d/furniture.js is dead code. decorate.js is used only by the index.html tool (src/main.js:14,320), not the game. The cleanest seam is a render-only "dress" pass in room_view.assemble(). It keeps every procedural mesh as an invisible but still raycastable proxy (material swapped to a shared MeshBasicMaterial with visible:false). It adds a GLB normalized and scaled to the proxy's local bbox as a child Group, excluded from raycasts (layers.set(1) plus cam.layers.enable(1)). I checked the r128 vendor code: Raycaster filters by layers only (not material.visible); the render list and shadow pass skip material.visible=false, so they skip the proxies; the shadow pass tests object layers against the main camera, so the layer-1 GLB still casts shadows.

hooks.how: Right after `if (!built || !built.room) throw` and BEFORE `dimRoomMaterials(built)`, call a new render-only `await dressFurniture(built, roomDef, {loadGLB, AT})` from a new module src/render3d/furniture_dress.js. Map each built.furniture child with userData.uid+size to a preset, using roomDef.furniture.find(f=>f.uid===uid).preset (same lookup as furnInfo 5959-5962) or userData.type, then look it up in a new data/furniture_visuals.json (preset → glb, yaw, fit, keep[]). Running before dimRoomMaterials means FURN_DIM 0.78 also applies to the GLB materials. assemble() runs on every rebuild (commitFurnitureAt → rebuildRoom 6729, refreshFurniture 7268-7273, lamp moves 7252), so dress must be idempotent and use the cache.

Reuse loadGLB (_glbCache promise + scene.clone(true), so geometry/materials are shared) with AT('../../assets/furniture/gen/<preset>.glb') (AT defined :73). Preload during the boot 'room' progress phase. On load failure, leave the procedural meshes as they are (graceful fallback).

In the dress module: compute the proxy's LOCAL bbox from g's direct child meshes (geometry.boundingBox transformed by child.matrix, excluding g's rotation), not userData.size (bed size.h is 0.94 but the drawn bed is 0.583). Normalize the GLB bbox to min.y=0 and center x/z, apply the spec yaw so the front faces +Z (builder convention: drawer knobs/desk slots at +Z, headboard/chair back at -Z), then scale per axis to the proxy bbox. Wrap it in a Group {name:'dress', userData:{visualOnly:true}} and add it to g, not to g.parent, so rot/position/visibility follow. Only after the GLB is attached, swap each proxy mesh's material to ONE shared `new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({visible:false})`, keeping the original in userData.__dressOrig. Never set g.visible, never colorWrite=false, never transparent. Skip meshes with glowing emissive materials (lampShade parts).

hooks.what: Exclude GLB meshes from all raycasts
hooks.how: Add `ctx.cam.layers.enable(1)` and set every dress mesh to `layers.set(1)`. The r128 Raycaster tests layers (`t.layers.test(e.layers)&&t.raycast`), so ray, _srfRay (6474) and _dropRay (2921) keep hitting the layer-0 proxies. The shadow pass tests layers against the main camera, so the GLB still casts sun shadows. perf_notes: Renderer: scene.js creates WebGLRenderer(antialias:true) with setPixelRatio(min(2,dpr)), PCFSoft, sRGB output and ACES exposure 1.1 (scene.js:13-21). room_view overrides this for phones. On dpr≥2 it pre-creates a webgl2 context with antialias:false, stencil:false, alpha:false (room_view 707-713), so there is no MSAA on phones and an FXAA/SMAA pass is needed if post is added. Shadow type is PCFShadowMap (751), sun map 1024 (749), ceilingBulb 512 (750). Shadow mode 'lean' is the default: only the sun casts; sky portals and ceiling cube are off (4864-4889); the sun shadow camera is fitted to the room. Shadow maps are manual (autoUpdate=false, needsUpdate in updateLight scene.js:176-178). Pixel ratio = min(maxPixelRatio 1.75, dpr). autoQuality steps it down through [1.75, 1.5, 1.25, 1.0, 0.85] after two 500 ms windows below 24 fps (5319-5341); resize at 5343-5352. A composer must mirror setPixelRatio/setSize in both places. The render loop is on-demand (needsRender) with fps caps: idle 10, idle with a skeletal character 18, busy 30, move 60 with backoff (5054-5136). Continuous effects (dust motes, light-shaft shimmer) will force frames and fight the battery policy, so animate them at the idle cap or bake the motion. Render call sites to replace with a composer: 5230 (loop), 9647 (redraw), 10128. Current banjiha cost is about 103 draw calls / 76k tris (room_view comments 5089, 5102); the furniture builders total about 2.2k tris for 11 pieces. Meshy GLBs run about 5k+ tris with 2-5 MB textures (lamp_desk_mint 5,375 tris, 2.5 MB GLB + 5.4 MB PNG). Suggested phone budget: ≤10-15k tris per hero piece, one merged material per piece (one draw call), 1024 px (or smaller) textures embedded as JPEG/WebP, furniture total ≤100k tris. tools/test_perf_budget.mjs asserts the furniture blob stays 1 draw call and siru draw calls stay 47±6; tools/test_roomview_perf.mjs measures 390×844 dpr2 at CPU×4. Post-processing is vendored but not wired: vendor/three/postprocessing/{EffectComposer, RenderPass, SSAOPass, SAOPass, UnrealBloomPass, ShaderPass}; shaders {FXAA, Vignette, ColorCorrection, GammaCorrection, CopyShader}. At 390×844×1.75 (~683×1477 px), full-res SSAOPass re-renders the scene for normals and depth. Prefer half-res SAO/SSAO or rely on the existing contact blobs, and half-res bloom. Proxies with material.visible=false are skipped in those extra passes: r128 builds render lists with `material.visible&&push` before overrideMaterial, and the shadow pass also checks material.visible. Layer-1 dress meshes render only because cam.layers.enable(1). Verify r128 composer output handling: a RenderPass into a render target writes linear output (outputEncoding applies only to the default framebuffer), so a final GammaCorrection/output pass is needed to match the current sRGB+ACES look.

With N passes, 'fps' is inflated N×, so water fps >33 (:242) and the call counts are wrong. (a) POST-PROCESSING — headless speed. Headless runs on SwiftShader. SSAO and bloom at 390x844 dpr2 (pixel ratio up to 1.75) can push frames past 45 ms. test_uiwire settle()/F-A requires two rAFs in under 90 ms (:89-99, :388), and every CDP eval/tap flow slows down. autoQuality may drop the pixel ratio mid-test. Provide an FX-off switch for tests, or scale FX quality by pixel ratio.

(a) POST-PROCESSING — overlays. SSAO and bloom also hit the transparent overlays: heatmap (opacity 0.45), slot rings, the grid (LineSegments), placement ghosts (renderOrder 997-999, depthTest:false) and the select ring. The heatmap's red/blue readability and the ghost colors (GH_OK 0x4aa3ff, GH_NG 0xe8615a, good/ok/bad) are information and must survive the grade. check_shot_anomaly.py DARK_MEAN 15 and BORDER_FLAT 0.34 can flag vignetted night shots.

(a) POST-PROCESSING — load order and hosts. A darker floor (concrete or linoleum texture) can fail test_outside nbr_darker_than_room: our-room floor luminance must exceed the neighbor floor at t=0.5 and t=0.92 (:433-482). The floor under the heatmap (probe_lightview ⑤) and under the lamp (test_lampswitch B-3) also feeds pixel checks.

If procedural textures are generated in house.js/textures.js, the code runs in Node for every buildHouse: light_adapter rebuilds rooms many times, and test_floorlight already takes 24 s. Editing house.js or furniture_pastel.js also trips test_measured_fresh's section-B suspicion. Safer: generate textures in room_view after assemble, cached at module level.

(b) WALL/FLOOR MATERIALS — per-wall materials. Wall cutaway uses per-material clipping planes (house.js 'materials per face, don't share'; updateShellVisibility called in room_view.js updateCam 1627). New wall materials must stay per-wall instances with clipping preserved. dimRoomMaterials (room_view.js:662) and setLightPolicy (9676) re-color materials that have a .color. Textured materials must keep a color property, or the dimming and the 'house' comparison policy (probe_room_light) silently stop working.

(c) FURNITURE GLBs — without raycast proxies. If the GLB replaces the primitive meshes instead of hiding them, every raycast consumer changes. S-1/S-2/S-3/B-1..B-5/C-*/E-5/F-*/I-*/N-* in test_roomview_place break, as do Q-1..W-3 in test_place_grid. test_ground H (floating spots) breaks, test_lampswitch E-1 (lamp tap via pickLampRay) breaks, test_uiwire F-0..F-15 (tap-to-highlight via pickFurnitureAt) breaks, and test_quiet/test_place_confirm/test_siru_pick drag-drops break. Worst, free-placed pots get a different y, so their DLI changes (the hard rule is violated). meshRect uses per-mesh local bboxes, so a single merged GLB mesh would make the 'top rectangle' the whole object.

(c) FURNITURE GLBs — shared materials and emissive. highlightFurniture clones materials per mesh and skips meshes with emissive>0 (room_view.js:6000-6061). If every material of a GLB has non-zero emissive (common in exports), lit=0 and test_roomview_place L-1/L-5 and test_uiwire F-1 fail. GLB materials shared across instances are fine because it swaps per mesh, but dimRoomMaterials mutates shared materials (idempotent).

(c) FURNITURE GLBs — shadows vs the light calculation. Visible shadows cast by a GLB silhouette will differ from the calculation's box occluders. That is the 'screen ≠ calc' mismatch _render_vs_calc.html and _shadow_audit.html exist to catch. Choose deliberately: keep proxy boxes as the shadow casters (castShadow on proxies, material.visible=false still casts? NO — r128 skips invisible materials in the shadow pass, so if proxies are hidden the GLB must cast), and document the choice. New meshes need markShadow roles, or applyShadowPolicy warns.

(c) FURNITURE GLBs — async loading. Loading is asynchronous and the room is re-assembled on every furniture commit (light_adapter rebuilds). Attach from a cached template synchronously when possible, and never console.error on a load failure (test_sfx boot, test_lampmove H). test_roomview_place L-1/L-2 run inside one synchronous eval, so they tolerate a late attach, but screenshots can catch half-attached rooms (START-HERE §2.9-③).

(c) PROPS AND VFX — raycast blocking. Props or VFX placed on tops or in built.room with raycasting enabled can block surfaceAt at slot centers (S-1) or turn the top-of-canvas wall drop in test_quiet (:110-116) into a valid spot. Always disable raycast on decorative-only meshes.
